questions.question: What is the primary purpose of ‘sorting and searching emails’ when using email services?
questions.questionHtml: What is the primary purpose of ‘sorting and searching emails’ when using email services?

options.text: Organising emails based on various criteria for easy retrieval
options.html: Organising emails based on various criteria for easy retrieval

options.text: Sending emails to multiple recipients simultaneously
options.html: Sending emails to multiple recipients simultaneously

options.text: Changing the background colour of email messages
options.html: Changing the background colour of email messages

options.text: Creating animated GIFs to embed in email content
options.html: Creating animated GIFs to embed in email content

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Organising emails based on various criteria for easy retrieval.

Key Points

  • Sorting and searching emails help in organising emails based on various criteria such as date, sender, subject, or importance.
  • This functionality allows users to quickly retrieve relevant emails without manually sifting through their inbox.
  • Effective email organisation improves productivity and efficiency by ensuring important messages are easily accessible.
  • Many email services offer advanced search features, including filters and labels, to streamline email management.
  • Organising emails also helps in maintaining a clutter-free inbox, which can reduce stress and enhance user experience.

Additional Information

  • Email Filters
    • Email filters are automated rules that help in sorting incoming emails into different folders based on predefined criteria.
    • They can be set up to organise emails by sender, keywords, subject line, or other attributes.
    • Filters can also help in marking emails as read or assigning them specific labels for easy identification.
  • Email Labels
    • Labels are a way to categorise and tag emails for better organisation.
    • Unlike folders, multiple labels can be applied to a single email, providing more flexibility in email management.
    • Labels can be colour-coded to visually distinguish different categories of emails.
  • Search Operators
    • Search operators are special characters or commands used in the search bar to refine and narrow down search results.
    • Common search operators include "from:", "to:", "subject:", and "has:attachment".
    • These operators can significantly speed up the process of finding specific emails.
  • Archiving
    • Archiving emails removes them from the inbox without deleting them, making the inbox less cluttered while preserving important messages.
    • Archived emails can be easily accessed and searched whenever needed.
    • This feature is particularly useful for storing old but important emails that are not frequently accessed.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is Centers the contents on the page.

Key Points

  • Pressing Ctrl + E in MS Word 365 centers the text or content within the current paragraph or the selected text.
  • Center alignment is one of the four types of text alignment available in MS Word, alongside left alignment, right alignment, and justified alignment.
  • This shortcut is particularly useful for formatting titles, headings, or any content that needs to be visually centered on the page.
  • The centered text is aligned to the middle of the page, maintaining an equal distance from both the left and right margins.
  • Shortcut keys, such as Ctrl + E, enhance productivity by reducing the time required to navigate through menus for commonly used functions.
  • MS Word is widely used for text formatting and document creation, and mastering such shortcuts can significantly improve efficiency.

Additional Information

  • It selects the whole content on the file

  • Right aligns the contents on the page

    • Right alignment is often used for specific formatting needs, such as aligning dates or author names in formal letters.

questions.question: Which of the following is an effective method to handle SPAM emails?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is an effective method to handle SPAM emails?

options.text: Forward the email to all your contacts
options.html: Forward the email to all your contacts

options.text: Mark the email as SPAM or Junk
options.html: Mark the email as SPAM or Junk

options.text: Reply to the sender asking them to stop
options.html: Reply to the sender asking them to stop

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mark the email as SPAM or Junk.

Key Points

  • Utilize Your Email Provider's Spam Filters: Most email providers, such as Gmail, Outlook, and Yahoo Mail, have built-in spam filters. These filters analyze incoming emails based on various factors, including sender reputation, content, and links, to identify and block spam messages. You can often customize these filters to improve their accuracy.
  • Mark Spam Emails: When you receive a spam email, mark it as spam. This helps your email provider's spam filter learn and improve its ability to identify future spam messages.
  • Create a Filter Rule: You can create custom filter rules in your email client to automatically move emails from specific senders or with certain keywords to the spam or trash folder.
  • Unsubscribe from Unwanted Mailing Lists: Many spam emails come from mailing lists you may have inadvertently subscribed to. Look for an unsubscribe link at the bottom of the email and use it to unsubscribe.
  • Be Cautious of Phishing Emails: Phishing emails are designed to trick you into revealing personal information, such as passwords or credit card numbers. Be wary of emails that ask for personal information, contain suspicious links, or have urgent or threatening language.
  • Avoid Clicking on Links in Suspicious Emails: Never click on links in emails from unknown senders, even if they appear legitimate. Instead, type the website address directly into your web browser.
  • Keep Your Email Software Updated: Regularly update your email software to the latest version, as updates often include security patches and improved spam filtering capabilities.
  • Use a Strong Password for Your Email Account: A strong password makes it more difficult for hackers to gain access to your email account and send spam through it.
  • Consider Using a Spam Filter Service: If you're still receiving a lot of spam, you can consider using a third-party spam filter service. These services can provide additional layers of protection against spam.
  • Report Phishing Emails: If you receive a phishing email, report it to the appropriate authorities, such as the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) in the United States.

questions.question: Which of the following statements related to attaching a file to an email is correct?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statements related to attaching a file to an email is correct?

options.text: Writing a subject field is mandatory while sending an attachment.
options.html: Writing a subject field is mandatory while sending an attachment.

options.text: We can’t use CC field while sending an attachment.
options.html: We can’t use CC field while sending an attachment.

options.text: We can’t attach an audio file in an email attachment.
options.html: We can’t attach an audio file in an email attachment.

options.text: In Gmail, If your file is greater than 25 MB, Gmail automatically adds a Google Drive link in the email instead of including it as an attachment.
options.html: In Gmail, If your file is greater than 25 MB, Gmail automatically adds a Google Drive link in the email instead of including it as an attachment.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is In Gmail, If your file is greater than 25 MB, Gmail automatically adds a Google Drive link in the email instead of including it as an attachment.

Key Points

  • Gmail has a size limit for email attachments, which is 25 MB.
  • If an attachment exceeds 25 MB, Gmail automatically uploads the file to Google Drive, a cloud storage service provided by Google.
  • Once uploaded to Google Drive, Gmail includes a Google Drive link in the email instead of attaching the file directly.
  • This feature ensures that users can share large files seamlessly without encountering issues related to file size limitations.
  • Recipients can access the file through the provided link, which redirects them to Google Drive.
  • This integration between Gmail and Google Drive enhances the functionality of email services and provides a convenient solution for sending large files.
  • The file-sharing feature is part of Google’s ecosystem, which also includes services like Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides.

Additional Information

  • Writing a subject field is mandatory while sending an attachment
    • It is not mandatory to write a subject while sending an email with an attachment. However, it is a best practice to include a subject to provide clarity to the recipient.
  • We can't use CC field while sending an attachment
    • This statement is incorrect. The CC (Carbon Copy) field can be used in emails regardless of whether an attachment is included or not. It is used to send a copy of the email to other recipients.
  • We can't attach an audio file in an email attachment
    • This is incorrect. Audio files can be attached to emails as long as their size does not exceed the attachment limit (e.g., 25 MB for Gmail).

questions.question: Which of the following is / are parts of the standard Structure of Electronic mail?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is / are parts of the standard Structure of Electronic mail?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both Header and Body.

Key Points

  • Email, short for "electronic mail," is one of the most widely used features of the Internet, along with the web. It allows you to send and receive messages to and from anyone with an email address, anywhere in the world.

Additional Information

  • Email uses multiple protocols within the TCP/IP suite. For example, SMTP is used to send messages, while the POP or IMAP protocols are used to retrieve messages from a mail server. When you configure an email account, you must define your email address, password, and the mail servers used to send and receive messages. Fortunately, most webmail services configure your account automatically, so you only need to enter your email address and password. However, if you use an email client like Microsoft Outlook or Apple Mail, you may need to manually configure each account. Besides the email address and password, you may also have to enter the incoming and outgoing mail servers and enter the correct port numbers for each one.
  • The original email standard only supported plain text messages. Eventually, email evolved to support rich text with custom formatting. Today, email supports HTML, which allows emails to be formatted the same way as websites. HTML email messages can include images, links, and CSS layouts. You can also send files or "email attachments" along with messages. Most mail servers allow you to send multiple attachments with each message, but they limit the total size. In the early days of email, attachments were typically limited to one megabyte, but now many mail servers support email attachments that are 20 megabytes in size or more.

options.text: ‘Reply’ forwards email to specific contacts, while ‘Reply all’ forwards the original email to all contacts in the address book.
options.html: ‘Reply’ forwards email to specific contacts, while ‘Reply all’ forwards the original email to all contacts in the address book.

options.text: ‘Reply’ allows you to edit the original email’s content before sending the response, while ‘Reply all’ automatically includes the entire original email’s content in the response.

options.text: ‘Reply’ sends the response only to the original sender, while ‘Reply all’ sends the response to all recipients of the original email.
options.html: ‘Reply’ sends the response only to the original sender, while ‘Reply all’ sends the response to all recipients of the original email.

options.text: ‘Reply’ attaches any files from the original email, while ‘Reply all’ includes any attachments along with the entire original email’s content in response.
options.html: ‘Reply’ attaches any files from the original email, while ‘Reply all’ includes any attachments along with the entire original email’s content in response.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​‘Reply’ sends the response only to the original sender, while ‘Reply all’ sends the response to all recipients of the original email.

 Key Points

  • Using the TO Field: Under email etiquette, the TO field should contain the email's primary recipient(s). This field needs to contain the recipients who must respond to the email in order for it to be more accurate.
  • Add the recipients to the "To" field. Moreover, you can add recipients: in both the "Cc" and "Bcc" fields. When writing a message, including the contact's name in the text field along with the "+" or "@mention" symbol.
  • The "To" field is the recipient field that is the easiest to understand. It's intended for your email's primary recipients. These recipients should be the primary focus of your message.

 Additional Information

  • The Bcc (blind carbon copy) box in an email message allows you to send a duplicate of the message to a specific recipient while hiding their name from other recipients.
  • The Bcc box will show up whenever you create a message from the time you turn it on until you turn it off.
  • A copy of the email you are sending will also be sent to the email address you enter in the "carbon copy" or "CC" field.
  • The first line of text recipients sees when they open your email is the subject line.

questions.question: What does the Uniform Resource Locator (URL) specify?
questions.questionHtml: What does the Uniform Resource Locator (URL) specify?

options.text: Unique address assigned to each web resource
options.html: Unique address assigned to each web resource

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Unique address assigned to each web resource.

Key Points

  • Uniform Resource Locator (URL) is a reference or address used to access resources on the internet.
  • URLs are used to specify the location of a web resource on a computer network and a mechanism for retrieving it.
  • The format of a URL is defined in RFC 1738 by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF).
  • A URL typically consists of the protocol (such as HTTP or HTTPS), the domain name, and the path to the resource.
  • Examples include https://www.example.com or ftp://ftp.example.com/file.txt.

Additional Information

  • Components of a URL:
    • Protocol: Indicates the method used to access the resource, such as HTTP, HTTPS, FTP.
    • Domain Name: The human-readable address of the server hosting the resource, e.g., www.example.com.
    • Path: Specifies the exact location of the resource on the server, e.g., /folder/file.html.
    • Query String: Provides additional parameters for accessing dynamic content, e.g., ?id=123.
    • Fragment Identifier: Directs the browser to a specific part of a resource, e.g., #section2.
  • HTTP vs. HTTPS:
    • HTTP: HyperText Transfer Protocol, the standard protocol for transferring web pages.
    • HTTPS: Secure version of HTTP, encrypts data between the client and server.
    • HTTPS is critical for protecting sensitive data during online transactions.
  • Domain Name System (DNS):
    • DNS translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.
    • It functions like the internet's phone book, ensuring proper routing of web traffic.
  • Common URL Schemes:
    • HTTP: For accessing web pages.
    • HTTPS: Secure web page access.
    • FTP: File Transfer Protocol for downloading/uploading files.
    • MAILTO: For email addresses.
    • FILE: For accessing files on the local system.

questions.question: Which of the following internet services is a secure connection over the internet that allows users to connect to a private network from a remote location?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following internet services is a secure connection over the internet that allows users to connect to a private network from a remote location?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is VPN.

Key Points

  • A VPN (Virtual Private Network) creates a secure and encrypted connection over a less secure network, such as the internet.
  • It allows users to access a private network and share data remotely through public networks as if their computing devices were directly connected to the private network.
  • VPN services are widely used for enhanced security and privacy on the internet, protecting data from eavesdroppers and hackers.
  • Businesses use VPNs to secure remote access for employees working from different locations.

Additional Information

  • Encryption:
    • Encryption is the process of converting data into a code to prevent unauthorized access.
    • VPNs use encryption protocols to ensure that data transmitted over the internet is secure.
  • Tunneling:
    • Tunneling is the method used by VPNs to encapsulate and secure data packets as they travel over the internet.
    • It involves the creation of a secure 'tunnel' through which data is transmitted.
  • Types of VPNs:
    • Remote Access VPN: Allows users to connect to a private network from a remote location.
    • Site-to-Site VPN: Connects entire networks to each other, typically used by businesses with multiple locations.
  • VPN Protocols:
    • PPTP (Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol): One of the oldest VPN protocols, known for its speed but less secure.
    • L2TP/IPsec (Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol with IPsec): Provides stronger security than PPTP.
    • OpenVPN: Known for its strong security and open-source nature.

questions.question: A User Interface is the part of _______ that allows the user to enter and receive information.
questions.questionHtml: A User Interface is the part of _______ that allows the user to enter and receive information.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is operating system.

Key Points

  • Computer software includes both system and application software, and it's the component that enables user interaction through a user interface.

    • The UI can be graphical (GUI) or text-based (CLI), and is present in operating systems, apps, and other programs.

      • Operating systems like Windows, Linux, macOS.
      • Applications like Microsoft Word, Google Chrome, VLC Media Player.
      • Mobile apps and development tools.

Additional Information

  • Operating System is a type of system software that manages hardware and provides core UI elements like taskbars, file explorers, etc.
  • Computer Network refers to interconnected systems that share resources but are not the source of UI themselves.
  • Hardware refers to the physical components like keyboard, monitor, CPU – which are used by UI but do not provide it themselves.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the file formats used for web graphics?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is one of the file formats used for web graphics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is .gif.

Key Points

  • For web graphics .gif formats are used.
  • There are three file formats for graphics used on the web: JPG, GIF, and PNG.
  • The GIF and PNG image formats use what is called "index-colour".
    • They store a minimized colour palette in the image file and keys to where those colours should be located in the image.
    • File size for GIF and PNG images is generally related to the number of colours used. Commons numbers of colors are: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256.
    • The GIF and PNG image formats are ideal for images with flat colours (no gradients) and hard edges.
    • Common examples of these types of images are logos, logotypes, and illustrations without gradients.
  • The JPG image format was designed to efficiently store and compress realistic images and artwork (both in colour and greyscale).
    • The JPG format does a very good job of compressing images with lots of colours and gradations in colours. 
    • The JPG format is not capable of saving any transparency.
    • When saving images in the JPG format, you can choose the level of compression to balance the file size and image quality. The file
    • size is directly related to the actual size (in pixels) of the image. 

Additional Information

  • A file with the DOCX file extension is a Microsoft Word Open XML Format Document file.
    • DOCX files are used for everything from resumes and cover letters to reports, flyers, documentation, invitations, newsletters, and more.
  • TXT is a file extension for a text file, used by a variety of text editors.
    • There is no standard definition of a text file, though there are several common formats, including ASCII (a cross-platform format), and ANSI (used on DOS and Windows platforms).
    • TXT stands for TeXT.
  • The .exe file extension is short for “executable.”
    • These files are most commonly used on Windows® computers to install or run software applications.

questions.question: Which of the following is the function of an IP address?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the function of an IP address?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Identifying devices on a network.

Key Points

  • An IP address (Internet Protocol address) is a unique identifier assigned to each device connected to a computer network that uses the Internet Protocol for communication.
  • IP addresses are used to identify and locate devices on a network, ensuring that data packets reach the correct destination.
  • There are two types of IP addresses: IPv4 and IPv6. IPv4 addresses are 32-bit numbers, while IPv6 addresses are 128-bit numbers.
  • IP addresses are essential for the functioning of the internet, as they allow devices to communicate with each other by transmitting data packets.

Additional Information

  • Dynamic vs. Static IP Addresses
    • A dynamic IP address is assigned by a network when a device connects and can change over time.
    • A static IP address is manually assigned to a device and does not change over time.
  • Private vs. Public IP Addresses
    • Private IP addresses are used within a private network and are not routable on the internet.
    • Public IP addresses are used for communication over the internet and are unique across the entire web.
  • Network Address Translation (NAT)
    • NAT is a method used to modify network address information in IP packet headers while in transit, allowing multiple devices on a local network to share a single public IP address.
    • This is commonly used in home and small office networks.
  • Subnetting
    • Subnetting is the practice of dividing a network into smaller, more manageable sub-networks, or subnets.
    • This helps improve network performance and security by isolating different segments of the network.

questions.question: Which of the following types of networking is used to connect all the computers within a school or within an office?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following types of networking is used to connect all the computers within a school or within an office?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Local Area Network.

Key Points

  • A Local Area Network (LAN) is a type of network designed to connect computers and devices within a localized area such as schools, offices, or homes.
  • LANs are typically confined to a single building or a group of buildings and are used to share resources like files, printers, and internet access efficiently.
  • They are characterized by high data transfer speeds and low latency compared to other types of networks.
  • LANs can be established using wired connections (e.g., Ethernet) or wireless connections (e.g., Wi-Fi), depending on the network requirements.
  • LANs are crucial for enabling communication and collaboration in environments such as educational institutions, corporate offices, and small businesses.

Additional Information

  • Metropolitan Area Network (MAN):
    • A MAN is a network that spans a city or a large campus, linking multiple LANs together.
    • It is larger than a LAN but smaller than a Wide Area Network (WAN).
    • Examples include networks connecting offices in a city or university campuses spread over a large area.
  • Wide Area Network (WAN):
    • A WAN is a network that covers a broad geographical area, such as a country or even continents.
    • The internet itself is the largest example of a WAN.
    • It often uses telecommunications infrastructure like leased lines, satellite links, or fiber optics.
  • Personal Area Network (PAN):
    • A PAN is a very small network used for personal devices like smartphones, laptops, and wearable devices.
    • Examples include Bluetooth connections and USB tethering.
  • Advantages of LAN:
    • LANs offer cost-effective and efficient resource sharing, such as printers and centralized data storage.
    • They are secure due to limited coverage and controlled access points.
    • Maintenance and troubleshooting are easier due to the localized nature of the network.

questions.question: What does the term HTTPS mean?
questions.questionHtml: What does the term HTTPS mean?
questions.solution:
Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS) 

  • It is the protocol where encrypted HTTP data is transferred over a secure connection. It ensures data security over the network - mainly public networks like Wi-Fi.
  • By virtue, HTTPS encryption is done bi-directionally, which means that the data is encrypted at both the client and server sides. Only the client can decode the information that comes from the server. So, HTTPS does the encryption of data between a client and a server, which protects against eavesdropping, forging of information, and tampering of data.

questions.question: The term 'ISP' stands for __________, in the context of internet architecture.
questions.questionHtml: The term 'ISP' stands for __________, in the context of internet architecture.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Internet Service Provider.

Key Points

  • Internet Service Provider (ISP) is a company that provides individuals and organizations access to the internet and other related services.
  • ISPs may also provide a variety of services including web hosting, email, domain registration, and more.
  • ISPs operate at different levels: Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3, depending on their scale and the infrastructure they own.
  • Examples of major ISPs include companies like Comcast, AT&T, Verizon, and smaller local providers.

Additional Information

  • Internet Service Protocol (ISP):
    • This is not a correct term in the context of internet architecture. The proper term is Internet Protocol (IP), which is a set of rules governing the format of data sent over the internet or local network.
    • IP is one of the main protocols in the Internet Protocol Suite, and it is used to deliver packets from the source host to the destination host based on their IP addresses.
  • International Service Provider:
    • This term is not commonly used in the context of internet architecture. An ISP that operates internationally would simply be referred to as an international ISP.
    • These ISPs provide internet services across multiple countries and regions, often collaborating with local ISPs to provide comprehensive coverage.
  • Intranet Service Provider:
    • This term is also not commonly used. Intranet refers to a private network accessible only to an organization's staff.
    • An intranet service provider would be a company that assists in setting up and maintaining these private networks within an organization.
  • Internet Service Provider (ISP):
    • An ISP is a company that provides customers with Internet access. The ISP connects to its customers using a data transmission technology appropriate for delivering Internet Protocol datagrams, such as dial-up, DSL, cable modem, wireless or dedicated high-speed interconnects.
    • ISPs may also provide other services such as email, domain registration, web hosting, and data center services.
    • Examples include major companies like Comcast, AT&T, and Verizon, as well as smaller local providers.

questions.question: Which was the first programmable general purpose computer in the world?
questions.questionHtml: Which was the first programmable general purpose computer in the world?
questions.solution: ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer) was the first programmable general-purpose computer, designed by John Presper Eckert and John Mauchly at the University of Pennsylvania. Completed in 1945, it was used for various scientific calculations including the hydrogen bomb development and weather prediction. ENIAC used vacuum tubes and could perform 5,000 additions per second, making it a significant advancement over earlier mechanical computers. It demonstrated the potential of electronic computing, influencing many future computer designs, and marked the beginning of the electronic computing era, having a profound impact on science and technology.

questions.question: Which protocol is commonly used for sending emails from a client to a server?
questions.questionHtml: Which protocol is commonly used for sending emails from a client to a server?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP).

Key Points

  • Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP)
    • Function: Primarily used for sending emails from one server to another.   
    • Delivery Focused: It's specifically designed to handle the transmission of emails between mail servers.   
    • Push Protocol: Emails are "pushed" from the sender's server to the recipient's server using SMTP.   

Additional Information

  • Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP)
    • Function: Allows users to access and manage emails remotely on a mail server.   
    • Synchronization: Enables email synchronization across multiple devices (e.g., computer, phone, tablet).   
    • Server-Side Operations: Many operations (like deleting, moving, and flagging emails) are performed directly on the server.   
    • Flexibility: Offers more advanced features like searching and filtering emails directly on the server.   
  • Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP)
    • Function: The foundation of data communication on the World Wide Web. It's used to transfer web pages, images, and other resources between web servers and web browsers.   
    • Client-Server Model: Based on a request-response model where the client (browser) requests a resource, and the server responds with the requested data.   
    • Stateless: Each request and response is independent of previous interactions.   
  • Post Office Protocol (POP3)
    • Function: Primarily used for retrieving emails from a mail server to a local device.   
    • Download and Deletion: Typically, emails are downloaded to the local device and deleted from the server.   
    • Limited Synchronization: Less suitable for synchronizing emails across multiple devices.

questions.question: What icon is used for attaching a file or document to an email message?
questions.questionHtml: What icon is used for attaching a file or document to an email message?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Paper clip icon.

Key Points

  •  Paper Clip Icon: Used to attach files to a cell, allowing you to link external documents or images to your spreadsheet.
  • Pen Icon: Indicates that a cell is in edit mode, allowing you to modify its contents directly.
  • Smiley Icon: Represents a formula or function that has been entered into a cell, typically used for calculations or data analysis.
  • Trash Can Icon: Used to delete a selected cell, row, or column from the spreadsheet.
  • Comment Icon: Indicates that a comment has been added to a specific cell, providing additional notes or explanations.

 Additional Information 

  • The "send" part of an email typically specifies the email server.
  • The email server is responsible for sending, receiving, and storing emails.
  • It is a crucial component of the email infrastructure, handling the routing of messages between different users and domains.
  • The email server information includes details such as the outgoing (SMTP) server address. 
  • 1. User Name:
    • This is generally associated with the email account and is used for authentication when logging into the email system. It's often part of the email address (e.g., username@example.com).
  • 2. Email Server:
    • The email server is a computerized system that manages email. It has two main components:
    • Incoming Mail Server (IMAP or POP3): Responsible for receiving emails. IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) and POP3 (Post Office Protocol) are two common protocols used for this purpose.
    • Outgoing Mail Server (SMTP): Responsible for sending emails. When you send an email, your email client connects to the SMTP server to dispatch the message.
  • 3. Email Client:
    • An email client is a software application that allows users to send and receive emails. Examples include Microsoft Outlook, Mozilla Thunderbird, and Apple Mail. The email client interacts with the email server to manage emails.
  • 4. Organization Name:
    • This is typically not specified in the "send" part of an email. The organization name is more associated with the sender's information within the email content or signature. The email server, however, handles the routing and delivery of emails without necessarily specifying the organization name in the sending process.

When you send an email, your email client uses the specified email server to send the message to the recipient's email server. The recipient's email client then retrieves the email from their email server using the incoming mail server. This process is facilitated by standardized protocols like SMTP, IMAP, and POP3.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of an optical disk?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT an example of an optical disk?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is PROM.

Key Points

  • PROM stands for Programmable Read-Only Memory.
    • Read-only memory (ROM) is a type of memory that is used in electronics and computers.
    • It is a non-volatile memory, that is, information stored in such memory is permanent and cannot be changed.
  • DVD:
    • It stands for Digital Versatile Disc or Digital Video Disc.
    • It is a digital optical disc storage format invented and developed in 1995 and released in late 1996.
    • The medium can store any kind of digital data and is widely used for software and other computer files.
    • It offers 4.7 GB (single-sided, single-layer – common), 8.5 GB (single-sided, double-layer), 9.4 GB (double-sided, single-layer), 17.08 GB (double-sided, double-layer) storage capacity.
  • Blu-ray Disc (BD):
    • It is a digital optical disc data storage format.
    • It can store several hours of video in high-definition (HDTV 720p and 1080p).
    • The main application of Blu-ray is as a medium for video material such as feature films and for the physical distribution of video games for the PlayStation 3, Xbox One etc.
  • CD: 
    • It stands for Compact Disc.
    • It is a digital optical disc data storage format that was co-developed by Philips and Sony and released in 1982.
    • It offers a storage capacity of 700 MB.

Hence PROM is not an example of Optical Disk.

questions.question: In which of the following modes of data transmission, can the data flow in both directions simultaneously?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following modes of data transmission, can the data flow in both directions simultaneously?
questions.solution: Full-duplex mode of data transmission allows data to flow in both directions simultaneously, making it faster for large amounts of data. It is used in situations where there is a need for real-time communication. Simplex mode allows data to flow in only one direction, while half-duplex mode allows data to be sent in both directions, but not at the same time.
